chocolate.name: Chocolate

sections.whatItOffers: Chocolate, dark, 70–85% cacao solids: 1 oz gives about 170 calories, with magnesium (about 21%), iron (about 19%), zinc (about 12%) and 3.1 g of fiber. Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Eat a small piece on its own, or chop into porridge, yoghurt and baking.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for chocolate; this profile covers what it provides nutritionally, as part of a varied diet. Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS); this serving has about 3.4 mg.
